RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "General advice says begin cooperatively." / "Parent uses TFT2 (forgive single defection)." / "We can design a strategy that: - Uses TFT2 as base"
STRATEGY: Parent uses tit-for-two-tats with endgame defection and retaliation; trace simulates TFT2, probing, and exploitation against pure cooperators/retaliators; proposes adding controlled probes and adaptive endgame defection.

--- PART 2/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Use these general suggestions while pursuing the stated tournament objective."
STRATEGY: The parent is a TFT2-like strategy that cooperates unless the opponent defected on the last two rounds or the opponent's total defections are at least 3 and at least half the rounds. The trace simulates this parent against probes and periodic defections, finding it tolerates sparse defection but retaliates to consecutive defections or a high defection rate. It proposes an adaptive strategy that starts cooperatively, probes with a single defection, then exploits non-retaliators with periodic defections while reverting to TFT2-style cooperation if the opponent retaliates.

--- PART 3/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report / "Use these general suggestions while pursuing the stated tournament objective." / "The general advice says a conciliatory action can help end alternating retaliation."
STRATEGY: Parent is a TFT2-like strategy that defects on two consecutive opponent defections or when opponent defections are at least half of rounds. The trace simulates parent against a probe/every-third-D exploitation and against slot0, always-D, pure-C, and slot5. It changes the revised strategy to probe at n=10, exploit every third round, test double-D at n=30-31, then defect all if no retaliation, while using TFT2-like forgiveness in retaliation mode.

--- PART 4/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: "kept using the report" — "The archive might contain grim, but the general advice says to avoid permanent retaliation. We can assume grim is rare." and "So double D test is safe."
STRATEGY: Parent uses TFT2-like cooperation with endgame defection; simulated against pure C, always D, TFT, parent, and slot5; changed to exploit non-retaliators via periodic D, double-D test, then all-D, while retaining TFT2 mode after opponent defection.
